name: AlwaysInDirection
quote: always in: If you have to be in the market at all times, either long or short, this is whatever your current position is... With trend: In general, the direction of the most recent 5 minute chart signal should be assumed to be the trend's direction. Also, if most of the past 10 or 20 bars are above the moving average, trend setups and trades are likely on the buy side.
description: Global regime concept gating every entry: the market's presumed always-in direction, read here as a proxy -- bullish when most of the last N bars closed above the EMA, else bearish. A design decision is needed before this can be coded exactly as Brooks means it (the most recent significant signal's direction).
pseudocode: countCloseAboveEma(lookback) >= majorityFraction * lookback
book_order_type: n/a (global context filter used to permit/deny with-trend vs countertrend entries)

complexity.reason: Brooks defines always-in by trader judgment of the 'most recent signal'; the bar-count-above-EMA proxy is one of several possible codings and needs a design decision

notes: MINING.md cites this exact concept as the canonical research-grade example.

name: DeepPullbackTreatedAsNewTrend
quote: the odds that a pullback will get back to the prior trend's extreme fall substantially if the pullback retraces 75 percent or more. For a pullback in a bear trend, at that point, a trader is better off thinking of the pullback as a new bull trend rather than a pullback in an old bear trend.
description: Filter: once a countertrend pullback has retraced at least X% of the prior trend's range (trend start to trend extreme), stop assuming with-trend continuation is likely and instead treat the pullback as a possible new trend in the opposite direction.
pseudocode: retracement = (trendExtreme - close[0]) / (trendExtreme - trendStart); retracement >= deepRetracementFraction

complexity.reason: needs the remembered start and extreme of the identified prior trend leg

name: AlwaysInTrendContext
quote: “Always in” ... means that if you had to be in the market at all times, either long or short, the always-in position is whatever your current position is.
description: Shared primitive: a persistent regime state, whether the market's inferred ‘always-in’ direction is long or short. Used throughout the chapter to gate which side of a breakout is with-trend. Coded here as a simple EMA-side proxy; a real implementation may prefer a design-level always-in variable shared across chapters.
pseudocode: close[0] > ema(emaLength)[0]

complexity.reason: ‘always-in’ is a persistent regime concept Brooks reserves for detailed treatment in book 3; any single-bar or EMA-side proxy is a design decision, not a direct mechanization.

notes: Every other RP1 candidate that says ‘in a bull trend’ or ‘in a bear trend’ depends on this primitive.

name: TrendDayWithTrendOnly
quote: at that point the day was clearly a bear trend day and traders should only be shorting unless there was a clear and strong long scalp
description: Filter: on a trend day (session close-to-date far from session open, most closes on one side of the EMA), take only with-trend entries.
pseudocode: (close[0] - sessionOpen) >= trendDayAtr * atr(atrLookback) && fractionOfSessionBarsAboveEma >= minFraction  (bull trend day; allows longs only)

complexity.reason: 'trend day' needs a design decision; the pseudocode is one proxy

name: CountertrendOnlyAfterPriorStrengthNearMagnet
quote: When a market is trending toward a magnet, it is prudent to trade with the trend until the magnet is tested and preferably overshot. Do not trade countertrend at the magnet unless there has been some prior countertrend strength like a trend line break, or unless the move is a pullback in a higher time frame trend.
description: Filter, generalized from R08-15: at any magnet level, permit a countertrend entry only if there was prior countertrend strength (e.g. an earlier trend-line break) or the move is itself a pullback within a higher-time-frame trend.
pseudocode: atMagnetLevel && (R08-15 || pullbackInHigherTimeframeTrend)

complexity.reason: 'magnet level' is generic across the many families listed in this chapter, and 'higher time frame trend' needs a design decision

notes: Umbrella restatement of R08-15 applied to every magnet type in this chapter, not just the measured-move target.

name: ConsecutiveClimaxesImplyCountertrendCorrection
quote: Consecutive climaxes are usually followed by at least a two-legged countertrend move and often a reversal.
description: Filter: after two or more consecutive climactic spikes (each a burst of several same-direction trend bars) with minimal intervening pullback, expect at least a two-legged countertrend move of a minimum duration -- withhold fresh with-trend entries and look for the countertrend setup instead.
pseudocode: climaxCount(spikeBars, bodyFraction) >= minConsecutiveClimaxes

complexity.reason: 'climax' classification and leg-counting the resulting correction are both unresolved design decisions

name: CountertrendMicroSignalMustFailFirst
quote: High 1 and low 1 patterns are with-trend setups, so if one occurs within a pullback in a trend but in the direction of the pullback and not the trend, do not take the trade. Instead, wait for it to fail and then enter with the trend on the breakout pullback.
description: If a High 1/Low 1-shaped bar forms in the direction of a pullback (against the larger trend) rather than with the trend, do not trade it directly; require it to fail first, then take the resulting with-trend breakout-pullback entry instead.
pseudocode: counterTrendCountBar(R17-01) -> do not enter directly; wait for FailedBreakoutReversalEntry-style continuation with the trend
book_order_type: n/a (redirects the trade to the with-trend breakout-pullback entry)

complexity.reason: requires knowing the larger trend direction plus the breakout-pullback primitives from chapter 5

notes: References R05-02/R05-04 (ranges chapter 5's breakout-pullback entries).

name: AvoidNaiveReversalPatternCountertrendEntry
quote: It is a mistake to see every top or bottom as a great reversal setup, because if you take all of those countertrend entries, the majority of your trades will be losers... However, if you are selective and look for other evidence that a trend might reverse, these can be effective setups.
description: Because double tops/bottoms and head-and-shoulders patterns are trading ranges that continue the larger trend far more often than they reverse it, do not take every countertrend breakout of one of these patterns (R20-02/R20-04); only take it when there is additional selective evidence that the trend might actually reverse.
pseudocode:
// research: 'other evidence' that a trend might reverse is left undefined in this chapter
allowCountertrendReversalEntry = (isDoubleTop[0] || isHeadAndShouldersTop[0]) && reversalConfidenceScore[0] >= reversalConfidenceThreshold;
book_order_type: n/a (gates whether R20-02/R20-04 may be taken at all)

name: AlwaysInFlipEntry
quote: As a general rule, as soon as traders decide that there is now a bull trend underway, they should buy at least a small position at the market or on a tiny pullback... because the directional probability of an equidistant move is probably at least 60 percent.
description: As soon as the always-in direction is judged to have flipped to long, buy at least a small position immediately (at market, or on a minor pullback) rather than waiting for a full pullback entry, since the directional probability of an equidistant move is judged to be materially above 50%.
book_order_type: market order, or a limit order on a minor (sub-bar or lower-timeframe) pullback

complexity.reason: "always-in direction" is the MINING.md canonical research-grade example -- a design decision is needed before the flip itself can be detected at all

name: AvoidFading1MinuteBarsFilter
quote: You should rarely, if ever, fade off 1 minute bars, because the 3 and 5 minute bars provide better winning percentages.
description: Do not take fade (countertrend scalp) entries when the chart's bar interval is 1 minute; prefer 3-minute or 5-minute bars for these setups.

name: NoCountertrendInSteepTrendUnlessPriorBreakOrOvershoot
quote: if there is a steep trend, never trade countertrend, even if there is a high or low 2 or 4, unless there was first a prior significant trend line break or trend channel overshoot and reversal.
description: Block any countertrend entry (including counting setups like high2/high4) while the trend is steep, unless a significant trend-line break or a trend-channel overshoot-and-reversal has already occurred first.

// research/hard: 'steep trend' and 'significant trend line break' need a trend-line/channel-line projection and a slope threshold
allowCountertrendEntry = !isSteepTrend[0] || priorSignificantTrendLineBreak[0] || priorTrendChannelOvershootReversal[0];

complexity.reason: needs a trend-steepness measure plus trend-line/channel-line break and overshoot detection from pivots

name: AlwaysInFlipPrimitive
quote: When a bull trend bar that is not particularly large flips the market to always-in long, buy on a limit order at one tick above the high of the bar before it...
description: Shared primitive: the always-in direction flips to long when a bull trend bar closes in a way that makes a continued down move implausible to most traders (a design decision left to the authoring pass); flips to short on the mirror bear trend bar.
pseudocode:
// research: 'always-in' has no bar-level definition in this chapter; this is the corpus-wide always-in design decision
alwaysInFlippedLong[0]; // true on the bar the always-in direction becomes long

complexity.reason: 'always-in' is explicitly flagged as a research-grade concept requiring a design decision before it can be coded

name: BuyFadeUnconfirmedAlwaysInFlipDown
quote: When there is a bear spike in a bull market and the bears need the next bar to be a bear bar to confirm a flip of the always-in trade to down, buy the close of the last bear trend bar in the spike before the follow-through bar forms, at and below the low of the bear trend bar, and at the close of the next bar if it does not have a bear body (and buy on a stop above its high). A pullback is more likely than a bear spike and channel.
description: During a bear spike inside a bull market that would need one more bear bar to confirm an always-in flip to short, buy at the close of the last bear trend bar, at/below its low, and -- if the following bar fails to close bearish -- at that bar's close as well (or on a stop above its high).
book_order_type: buy at the close of the bear bar, at/below its low, at the close of the next bar if it lacks a bear body, and on a stop above that next bar's high

complexity.reason: multi-condition setup combining the research-grade always-in-flip concept with a conditional next-bar body test and three different order placements

notes: Kept whole rather than split further since the three order placements (close, low, next-bar-conditional) are all part of one described trading plan.

name: FadeCountertrendScalpersLimitEntry
quote: In a strong bull trend, fade short scalps, since most will fail. When there is a strong bull trend and then a short scalp setup, buy on a limit order at two or three ticks above where the short scalpers are looking to take profits.
description: In a strong bull trend, when a short-scalp setup forms, place a buy-limit order a few ticks above the level where short scalpers would take profit (a fixed distance below the bear signal bar), expecting their scalp to fail.
book_order_type: buy limit order two or three ticks above the short scalpers' expected profit-take level

complexity.reason: combines a research-grade strong-trend context with a short-scalp-setup classification and a fixed-offset price projection

name: AvoidCountertrendScalpInStrongTrend
quote: Once you believe there is a trend, you must accept that 80 percent of reversal attempts will fail and evolve into flags. This makes it almost impossible for most traders to enter countertrend trades on stops and consistently make a profit.
description: Do not take a countertrend scalp entry against a trend judged to be strong; the large majority of reversal attempts fail and become flags (continuations) instead.

// research: 'strong trend' and 'reversal (countertrend) attempt' classification are not reduced to a bar-level test in this chapter
blockCountertrendEntry = strongTrendContext[0] && isCountertrendSignal[0];

name: ScaleInCountertrendAtFixedIntervalsFadingRangeExtreme
quote: I have a friend who is an expert at scaling into countertrend trades in channels... he would start to short on limit orders at the most recent swing high, and add to his position at the next one or two new highs in the channel, as long as each new entry was at least two points higher than the prior.
description: Fade the extreme of a channel or trading range with multiple countertrend units, adding another unit each time price makes a new extreme at least a fixed point/tick distance beyond the prior entry -- reliable only when the day/channel is not a strong trend.
book_order_type: additional sell limit at each new swing high at least minIntervalPoints above the prior entry

name: FadeCountertrendSignalDuringStrongOppositeTrend
quote: Bar 18 was a low 2 short setup, but the market was still in a strong bull channel and now was going sideways for six bars. This low 2 was likely to fail, so bulls bought its low for a scalp... Bar 16 was a low 1 short setup after five bull trend bars and therefore likely to fail. Bulls would have bought at the low of the bar.
description: A countertrend low 1/low 2 short setup (or high 1/high 2 long setup) that forms while the larger trend is still judged strongly in the opposite direction is likely to fail; fade it (take the with-trend side at the setup bar's extreme) instead of the literal countertrend signal.

// research: 'still in a strong bull channel/trend' is a context classification this chapter assumes but does not reduce to a bar-level test
isCountertrendSetup = lowNSetupPrimitive[0]; strongOppositeTrend = strongBullTrendContext[0]; fadeShort = isCountertrendSetup && strongOppositeTrend; allowLongAtSetupLow = fadeShort;
book_order_type: buy limit/stop at the failing countertrend setup bar's extreme

quote: After a bear channel that lasted 20 or 30 bars, the correction was likely to have at least half as many bars as a general rule.

name: CountertrendScalpPercentTarget
quote: When trading counter to a strong trend, the goal should be a scalp of 1 or 2 percent, since most countertrend trades just result in pullbacks that become with-trend entries.

book_order_type: n/a (a limit/profit-taking exit near a small percentage move)

name: FadeCountertrendInTrendFilter
quote: If it is in a trend, most attempts to reverse it will fail.
description: Block a long entry while the market classifies as a bear trend (MarketInTrend's short-side condition true), and mirror for shorts against a live bull trend.
pseudocode: !(MarketInTrend.bear)

complexity.reason: inherits MarketInTrend's design decision

chapter_title: The Spectrum of Price Action: Extreme Trends to Extreme Trading Ranges

name: TrendResumptionDayContext
quote: Whenever there is a strong trend on the open and then a tight trading range for several hours, the chances for a trend resumption day are good.
description: Session-level context filter: if the market opened with a strong trend and then entered a tight trading range for several hours, favor with-trend continuation entries in the opening trend's direction over fresh countertrend fades.
pseudocode: MarketInTrend(openBars) && MarketInTradingRange(rangeBarsAfterOpen) -> trendResumptionBias = openTrendDirection

complexity.reason: session day-type classification carried forward across bars is a design decision, built on two other research-grade primitives

notes: This is a preview of the 'trend from the open' and 'trend resumption day' patterns fleshed out later in the trilogy (Part IV of this book).
chapter_title: The Spectrum of Price Action: Extreme Trends to Extreme Trading Ranges

name: AlwaysInDirectionFilter
quote: This is a very important concept, and most traders should trade only in the always-in direction.
description: Block a long entry unless the always-in direction (T03-13) is currently up; mirrored for shorts.
pseudocode: alwaysIn > 0

complexity.reason: MINING.md's own example of a research-grade concept: 'always-in direction' needs a design decision before the state machine can be coded

chapter_title: Breakouts, Trading Ranges, Tests, and Reversals

name: AlwaysInFlipOnStrongReversal
quote: A single strong reversal that reverses many closes and lows, like bar 29, can flip the always-in direction.
description: Treat a very strong reversal bar (one whose close reverses the closes and lows/highs of many prior bars) as flipping the market's 'always-in' direction, downgrading the reliability of any still-open pullback setups (high 1/high 2, low 1/low 2) in the old direction.
pseudocode: ReversalBarStrengthByClosesBeyondPriorBars(closeLookback, highLookback) -> alwaysInDirection = sign(close[0] - open[0])

complexity.reason: 'always-in direction' is a design decision per the mining brief's own example; this chapter gives one concrete trigger for flipping it

notes: Bar 29's worked example reverses the closes of the prior 13 bars and the lows of the prior 12; kept generic rather than hard-coding those two numbers.
Brooks then expects trapped with-trend traders to place limit orders that themselves fail (high 1/high 2 as sell setups) -- narrative, not separately mined as a distinct bar-level test.

name: CountertrendNeedsPriorPush
quote: Before taking a countertrend trade, it is always better to see some evidence in the preceding several bars that the bulls were able to move more than just a couple of ticks above the prior bar.
description: Gate for a countertrend LONG: within the last N bars, at least one bar's high exceeded the previous bar's high by more than K ticks.
pseudocode: countTrue((high[i] - high[i+1]) > minPushTicks * tickSize for i in 1..lookback) >= 1

complexity.reason: window scan of adjacent-bar high differences

notes: Figure 10.1: the tight bear channel from bar 8 had no such push, so the bar 10 long was suspect.

name: AlwaysInLong
quote: The market is always-in long and they should not be looking to short, even though there will be many signals that look acceptable.
description: Context filter: the market is always-in long. Proxy: close above the EMA and the EMA rising, or a recent strong bull spike (>= spikeBars consecutive bull trend bars) with no strong bear spike since.
pseudocode: close[0] > ma && ma > ma[maSlopeBars] /* proxy; true always-in needs the spike/flip state machine */

complexity.reason: Brooks's always-in is a judgment that flips on strong spikes; a proxy must be chosen before it can be coded

notes: p253 gives the flip-to-short test: a strong bear spike that breaks below the channel and the EMA with follow-through, then a lower high with a bear signal bar (see T15-24).

name: NoCountertrendUntilAlwaysInFlips
quote: That will usually require a strong bear spike that breaks below the channel and below the moving average and has follow-through, and then has a lower high with a bear signal bar.
description: Filter for short entries in a bull channel: allowed only after (a) a bear spike of >= spikeBars consecutive bear trend bars closing below the trend line and the EMA, (b) at least one more bar of follow-through, and (c) a lower swing high with a bear signal bar. Until then, longs only.
pseudocode: spike = spikeBars consecutive bear trend bars with close < ma && close < trendLine; followThrough = close[spikeEnd-1] < close[spikeEnd]; lowerHigh = swingHigh(1).price < swingHigh(2).price formed after spike; spike && followThrough && lowerHigh && close[0] < open[0]

complexity.reason: defines the always-in flip; a multi-stage state machine across pivots, EMA and spike detection

notes: p273 restates it: in a tight bull channel do not short below a bar unless there was a climactic reversal after a breakout of the top, and even then wait for a sell-off followed by a lower high (T15-61).

name: CountertrendOnlyEarlyInDay
quote: If you are scaling into shorts in that bull channel, it is best to do this only in the first two-thirds of the day.
description: Time filter for countertrend channel entries: the bar's close time is before cutoffTime (two-thirds through the session). After it, only with-trend channel trades (buy below prior bar's low, above bull reversal bars at the EMA).
pseudocode: time[0] < cutoffTime

complexity.reason: single Time comparison

notes: Default assumes a 0930-1615 ET session; two-thirds is about 1400.

name: ScalpOnlyCountertrendOnMinimalMomentum
quote: since these are countertrend and there was only minimal countertrend momentum on the trend line breaks, these trades are not strong and should only be scalps.
description: When the trend-line break preceding a countertrend fade (T17-06) was itself small/slow, cap the trade's target to a scalp distance instead of a swing target.
pseudocode: (high[breakBar] - low[breakBar]) < minBreakAtrMultiple * atr(atrLength) -> exit at scalpTicks profit instead of a swing target

complexity.reason: a single ATR-relative size test on an already-identified break bar, then a fixed-tick target

chapter_title: Horizontal Lines: Swing Points and Other Key Price Levels

name: MiddayCountertrendTrapWithTrendReentry
quote: They were after 11:30 a.m., when there is often a strong countertrend move that traps traders out of the trend and into the wrong direction. This sets up a reliable with-trend trade that usually results in a new extreme and often lasts into the close.
description: Intraday: after cutoffTime (late morning), a countertrend move that closes through the EMA (trapping with-trend traders out) but then resumes in the original trend direction is a high-quality with-trend re-entry.
pseudocode: time[0] >= cutoffTime && low[0] <= ma && close[0] > ma
book_order_type: buy stop above the touch bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: a time gate plus an EMA touch-and-hold test

chapter_title: Horizontal Lines: Swing Points and Other Key Price Levels

name: AlwaysInLong
quote: It is when the market becomes clearly always-in long in the eyes of most traders if the trend is a new bull trend, or always-in short in the case of a new bear trend.
description: Shared primitive / context filter: the market is 'always-in long', meaning a trader forced to hold a position would hold a long. Brooks ties the flip to a strong breakout spike (see TP3-04). A design decision is needed: candidate proxies are (a) the last spike of N consecutive trend bars was bullish, (b) close above the EMA for the majority of the last M bars, (c) trending swings (TP3-08).
pseudocode: alwaysInLong = lastSpikeDirection == up  // proxy: the most recent run of spikeBars consecutive trend bars (TP3-04) closed up, and no opposite spike has since occurred

complexity.reason: 'always-in' is a discretionary read; a proxy must be chosen before it can be coded

notes: Gates most with-trend candidates in Chapters 18 to 20. Book 2 gives more detail; the dedup pass should merge all AlwaysIn definitions.

name: WithTrendOnly
quote: Depending on how you define a trend and a reversal attempt, about 80 percent of attempts to reverse a trend will fail.
description: Context filter: take entries only in the direction of the established trend (long side allowed when always-in long). Blocks all countertrend entries.
pseudocode: alwaysInLong

complexity.reason: inherits the always-in definition problem

notes: Concrete proxies: close > EMA(close, 20) for k of the last n bars; TP3-08 TrendingSwings.

name: AlwaysInLongBlocksShorts
quote: A trader can always be long, short, or flat. At any moment during a trend, only two of those choices are compatible with being a successful trader. If the market is in a bull trend, successful traders are only long or flat.
description: While the market is classified 'always-in long' (a bull trend is in effect), block new short entries and prefer flat over short.
pseudocode: // needs a design decision on how 'always-in direction' is classified from bars (the concept itself is central to the trilogy but never reduced to a formula here)
book_order_type: n/a (a global gate on entries, not itself an order)

complexity.reason: 'always-in direction' is the canonical example of a concept that needs a design decision before it can be coded (per MINING.md)

chapter_title: Example of How to Trade a Trend

name: NoPullbackForNBars
quote: the market will often go for five or more bars without a pullback.
description: None of the last N bars was a countertrend (bear) bar in a bull trend -- the trend has run N straight bars with no pullback at all.
pseudocode: countIf(i, 0, minBarsNoPullback - 1, close[i] < open[i]) == 0

complexity.reason: window loop over a per-bar open/close comparison

notes: Different from ConsecutiveUpBars: this only requires the ABSENCE of an opposite-direction bar, not that every bar close above its own open.
chapter_title: Signs of Strength in a Trend

name: ABCPullbackPattern
quote: There is a countertrend move, a small with-trend move that usually does not go beyond the trend's extreme, and then a second countertrend move that usually extends deeper than the first.
description: The classic three-step ABC pullback: leg A countertrend, leg B a small with-trend bounce that fails to exceed the trend's prior extreme, leg C a second countertrend move that goes deeper than leg A -- entry with the trend once leg C completes.
pseudocode: // legA = first countertrend leg since the trend's last extreme; legB.extreme < priorTrendExtreme (bull case: legB high stays below the swing high); legC.extreme beyond legA.extreme (deeper low); enter beyond the signal bar that ends legC
book_order_type: stop entry one tick beyond the signal bar ending leg C, mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open

complexity.reason: same leg-detection dependency as T20-02, plus an added constraint on leg B's extreme relative to the prior trend extreme

notes: A more specific, three-leg-with-constraints variant of T20-02; 'composite' since it names three distinct legs (composes T20-01 three times conceptually, listed once).

name: WithTrendOnlyOnTrendDay
quote: you should be trying to take every with-trend entry, no matter how weak the setup looks
description: Filter: when a trend-day pattern has been recognized (opening range small or large, per TP4-03/TP4-06), only allow entries in the day's trend direction. Long side: day trend is up.
pseudocode: trendDayRecognized && dayTrendUp

complexity.reason: depends on the research-grade DayTrendDirection primitive

notes: Corollary on page 354: if no pattern is recognized, assume a trading range day and allow both directions; that is simply this filter being false.

name: MaxCountertrendTradesPerSession
quote: you should not find more than two or three countertrend trades in the day
description: Filter: block a countertrend entry once the number of countertrend entries taken this session has reached the maximum.
pseudocode: countertrendEntriesThisSession < maxCountertrend  /* counter reset on Date change, incremented when an entry is filled against dayTrend */

complexity.reason: persistent per-session counter fed by position-history reads

name: VeryStrongTrendNoCountertrend
quote: In a very strong trend, all trades should be with-trend swings (scalping out part) and no trades should be countertrend scalps
description: Filter: when the trend is very strong (proxy: the close has stayed above the EMA for at least N consecutive bars), block any short entry; long side of the mirrored rule is 'trend is very strongly up, longs allowed'.
pseudocode: barsAboveEma = consecutive bars with close > ema(close, emaLength); barsAboveEma >= strongBars

complexity.reason: an EMA and a counter persisting between bars

notes: Chapter 21 page 365 gives the 20-bars-above-the-moving-average proxy for 'very strong'; used here as the default.

name: AlwaysInLong
quote: it signals that the market is breaking into a clear always-in situation
description: Research primitive: the market is always-in long. Proxy candidates: a bull spike has occurred and the close has not fallen below the spike start since; or close above the EMA with a higher low structure. Every with-trend-only filter in this chapter depends on it.
pseudocode: spikeSeenUp && lowest(low, barsSinceSpike) > spikeStart  /* or: close[0] > ema(close, 20) */

complexity.reason: 'always-in' is a judgment; the proxy is a design decision

notes: Page 358: 'As long as the pullback from the spike is not strong enough to flip the always-in trade to the opposite direction, the market will likely continue the trend' - the spike-start test is a reading of that.

name: NoCountertrendScaleInLateSession
quote: it is risky to scale into a countertrend position in a channel in the second half of the day, because you will often run out of time
description: Filter: countertrend entries are blocked once the session time is past a cutoff (the second half / final couple of hours of the day).
pseudocode: Time < countertrendCutoffTime

complexity.reason: a Time comparison

notes: Default is PST for the Emini session (06:30-13:15); adjust per instrument.

name: FailedCountertrendScalpWithTrendEntry
quote: The failures of these countertrend scalps are great with-trend setups. Just enter on a stop where the countertrend traders are exiting with their protective stops.
description: Entry: in a bull channel, a countertrend short was triggered (a bar fell below the low of a bear signal bar) and now a bar closes above that bear signal bar's high, where the shorts' stops sit; buy at the next open.
pseudocode: alwaysInLong && close[2] < open[2] /* bear signal bar */ && low[1] < low[2] /* short triggered */ && close[0] > high[2]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the bear signal bar high

complexity.reason: three-bar comparisons; context from the always-in filter

notes: Chapter 22 page 404 'failed high 2 ... low 2 short' is the same idea on the short side with a count.

name: BounceOfFixedSizeFromLow
quote: Some will buy on a stop two points above the low, seeing a bounce of that size as a sign that the reversal in underway.
description: Entry (countertrend, long side): after a decline, the close is at least a fixed distance (points or ATR multiple) above the lowest low of the last N bars.
pseudocode: close[0] >= lowest(low, lookback) + bounceAtr * atr
book_order_type: buy stop a fixed amount above the low

complexity.reason: window lowest plus ATR

notes: Brooks quotes 'two points' in the Emini; ATR scaling is the portable form.

name: AvoidEntryAtScheduledReportTime
quote: Computers have a huge edge on reports...therefore should rarely enter at the moment a report is released.
description: Filter: block new entries within a short window of a known recurring report time (e.g. 7:00 a.m. PST economic data); wait for the bar containing the report to close and for the always-in direction to become clear.
pseudocode: abs(Time - reportTime) <= reportBlockMinutes -> block new entries this bar

complexity.reason: a Time comparison, but the report time is instrument/market-specific and not itself in OHLCV data -- treated as a fixed recurring parameter

notes: One-off events like an FOMC announcement do not recur at a fixed daily time and cannot be captured this way; only regularly scheduled data releases fit this pattern.
chapter_title: Trend from the Open and Small Pullback Trends

name: TightMiddayRangePredictsResumption
quote: Whenever this happens and especially if the sideways action is in a very tight trading range, the day is likely becoming a trend resumption day.
description: Filter: after a qualifying morning trend leg (T25-02), the market has stayed inside a tight range for at least H hours; the tighter that midday range relative to the average daily range, the more likely a late-session resumption of the morning trend. Enables the trap-fade (T25-04) and blocks new countertrend entries.
pseudocode: morningLegDirection != 0 && barsSinceMorningLeg >= minMiddayBars && (middayRangeHigh - middayRangeLow) <= tightRangeFraction * avgDailyRange

complexity.reason: combines two stateful primitives plus a running midday range measurement

notes: Page 454: the midday action does not have to be a flat range -- a weakly trending countertrend move for a couple of hours that ultimately fails is a variant of this same setup; tightRangeFraction is a proxy for either form.
